To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the long-term administration of alcoholic beverages to rats together with inadequate diets does not cause severe liver lesions, especially not cirrhosis, in spite of a high mortality rate.
chronic alcohol consumption does not lead to cirrhosis in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of long-term administration on the liver of rats given alcoholic beverages, especially whisky, gin, red wine or brandy, in combination with different diets.
the effects of long-term administration to rats of different alcoholic beverages (whisky, brandy, gin and wine) together with hypocalorific (25 per cent) diets of different composition.
the effects of different alcoholic beverages on the rat liver, when they are given together with inadequate diets for several months.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alcohol, when given in adequate amounts, is not hepatotoxic in itself but that it may be hepatotoxic in the presence of other factors such as hypocaloric or hypovitaminic diets.
the liver lesions in rats given alcohol are due to the alcohol and not due to other components of the beverages.
alcohol per se, in the absence of other factors, is a non-toxic substance in rats and in man.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver of rats given alcoholic beverages in the above mentioned experiments did not show any significant difference in comparison with rats given glucose.
the liver damage caused by alcohol in the rat is due to the alcohol itself and not to congeners.
in rats, alcohol per se is a hepatotoxin only when it is given in high doses, and then only in combination with a low vitamin and low protein diet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a very important organ in the body, and it can be damaged by alcohol in a number of ways.
the liver can be damaged by drinking alcohol.
the liver is not damaged by alcohol consumption alone.
